frontier.hypothesis: Escape #8 (missing LOG_LINK) is the only escape that does NOT merge the record and links pseudos, so it is the only one whose seats can match target; its single measured defect is that cse eats the preheader's base add, and that defect may be removable without the t two-step by making the preheader's addend expression not cse-equivalent to the guard's.
frontier.mechanism: In cell S the base add died because sh2 + q canonicalises onto the guard's already-computed sh2 + p pseudo, which is still available. The t two-step removes the availability but costs the guard's own shape (Z2/Z3 = 40). An association or typing difference that makes the preheader's addend a DIFFERENT cse expression - e.g. the guard written over (slot_a << 6) + (s32)p while the preheader is written over (s32)q + sh2, or the count read done through a differently-typed lvalue - would keep the value unavailable without changing the guard's instructions.
frontier.next_probe: On the cell-S chassis (tmp/grind/func_80017848/s32/body_S.c) sweep the association/typing axis of the two addends only: guard (slot_a << 6) + (s32)p vs sh2 + (s32)p vs (s32)p + sh2, crossed with preheader sh2 + (s32)q vs (s32)q + sh2 vs pointer arithmetic q + sh2. Score each and, for every cell reaching 127 build insns, run s32/dis.sh and check whether addu a3,a0,zero appears BEFORE or AFTER the blez - the ordering, not the score, is the discriminator.

frontier.hypothesis: Cell AK's four-seat permutation (p a1->a0, sh a0->a1, q v0->a3, links a1->a2) is reachable by changing which pseudo cse promotes to canonical at the copy, because make_regs_eqv's promotion test is decided by variable first/last mention positions that are freely settable in C.
frontier.mechanism: cse.c:840-855 promotes the copy's destination to qty_first_reg only when it is first mentioned before the cse block start (or last mentioned past its end) AND outlives the source. Which register the base add reads, and hence which pseudo carries the value into local-alloc, follows from that promotion; the allocno ordering that produced AK's permutation is downstream of it. No session has tried steering the promotion on an escape-#9 chassis - s32 only observed it on cell S.
frontier.next_probe: On body_AK.c vary the copy destination between (a) a fresh local, (b) slots (first mentioned in the top guard block, i.e. before the loop-1 cse block starts), (c) rec_a or rec_b (mentioned only in the post-loop tail, i.e. last-mentioned past the block end) and (d) link. Score each and dump ings.cse2 for the promoted register; the prediction is that (b) and (c) move the base add's operand and with it the a3/v0 seat.

frontier.hypothesis: The three-insn combine path - can_combine_p(i1, i3, NULL, i2) refusing on `succ && ! all_adjacent && reg_used_between_p (dest, succ, i3)` at combine.c:902 - is the only can_combine_p refusal still never spelled, and unlike escapes 1, 2 and 9 it requires neither a second use nor the p/links pseudo merge.
frontier.mechanism: That refusal only fires when combine is attempting a THREE-insn combination, i.e. when the base add has TWO LOG_LINKS (one to the copy, one to another single-set feeder such as the shift). Target's base add does read two values (sh and q), so an i1/i2/i3 attempt is structurally available here; the refusal then needs the copy's destination used between i2 and i3, which is a placement question rather than an extra instruction.
frontier.next_probe: Build a cell whose loop-2 base add is fed by two combinable single-set feeders (the copy AND a freshly computed sh2 set in the same block, so both carry LOG_LINKS), with the lnk load placed between them, and read ings.combine for whether try_combine reports a three-insn attempt at that insn. If the attempt happens and is refused, measure the resulting seats; if no three-insn attempt is made, record that combine.c:902 is unreachable for this CFG and close the last can_combine_p path.
